label: Basis points
background: A basis point, shortened to bps, is a financial unit equal to one-hundredth of a percentage point (0.01%). It is used to clearly describe tiny changes in interest rates without confusing percentage math. Much like using precise integer units in software to avoid floating-point rounding errors, basis points provide a clear, unambiguous scale.
author_says: According to Bank of America (BofA), a 25 bps hike in October, rather than December as previously forecast, is possible due to higher energy prices, food inflation, and wider price pressures that strengthen the case for tighter policy.
